question: In which year was the Terapanth sector of Jain monastics founded?
answer: What the corpus does say: "They are recruited from all three sei-ts, though their founder was a Sthfinakavasi, who about 150 years ago, in Sojat ( Marwar ), entertained doubts about certain current practices, and founded a sect of his own. They are called Terapantha, because the number of Sadhus who joined was originally thirteen. Their ascetics wear the same dress, etc., as the Sthanakavasi Sadhu, but will not stay in an U" (Notes on Modern Jainism (1910) (Mrs. Sinclair Stevenson, 1910)). The corpus does not record a founding year for Terapanth, so this question cannot be answered from the available sources. Evidence needed first: a dated Terapanth foundation record.
